title: How to Use Autodesk Assistant in Revit 2026: Alternatives
summary: Autodesk Assistant requires Revit 2027 or later. Use ArchiLabs in Revit 2026 for native AI editing and evaluate a specification-to-model workflow.
body_markdown:
Autodesk Assistant isn't available in Revit 2026. Autodesk ships it with Revit 2027 and later ([Autodesk version availability](https://help.autodesk.com/view/RVT/2026/ENU/?caas=caas%2Fsfdcarticles%2Fsfdcarticles%2FHow-to-enable-Autodesk-Assistant-feature-available-in-Revit-2025.html) ). If you saw it in a demo and then couldn't find it in your own Revit, nothing is wrong with your installation.


That's frustrating when your project runs on 2026 and is likely to stay there for a while. The good news is that you don't need Autodesk's Assistant to get AI help with the model. ArchiLabs Desktop supports native model editing in Revit 2026, along with 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2027.


## How to use Autodesk Assistant in Revit 2026


In Revit 2026 itself, you can't. No setting or add-in enables the built-in Assistant in 2026 or earlier releases. To use Autodesk's version, the project has to open in Revit 2027 or later. To get AI help in the 2026 model you have now, you need a tool that supports 2026, such as ArchiLabs Desktop.


Keep those two choices separate, because they're different sizes of decision. One person can start trying AI-assisted modeling this week. Changing the Revit version of an active project involves everyone who works on the model.


## What Autodesk Assistant does in Revit 2027


It helps to know what you're missing before you weigh an upgrade. In Revit 2027, the Assistant answers help questions, queries the model and can modify it. Autodesk's[November update notes](https://www.autodesk.com/blogs/aec/2026/11/10/whats-new-in-revit-2027-3-and-2027-4/) describe schedule and graphics operations and traceability, delivered through Assistant service updates that now ship separately from Revit point releases. They also cover DynamoMCP, which in Revit 2027.3 with Dynamo 4.2.1 can build and run Dynamo graphs, and a public MCP Technical Preview with Read, Write and Experimental extensions. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard way for AI tools to connect to applications like Revit. If you read an older post that called Revit's AI tooling read-only, it's out of date.


## Should you upgrade the project?


For most active projects, the Assistant alone isn't a good enough reason. Revit upgrades a project file when a newer release opens it, and the upgraded file can't go back to the older version. Consultants sharing models usually need to be on the same release. That makes the move a project-wide decision about timing, add-ins and coordination. It's reasonable to plan an upgrade for a natural break in the project, and to get AI help in 2026 until then.


## AI modeling in Revit 2026 with ArchiLabs Desktop


ArchiLabs Desktop is a Windows application that works with native Revit and AutoCAD content and project files. You describe the task in a chat and attach whatever it needs: a manufacturer PDF, a spreadsheet, a marked-up screenshot, selected elements, or a narrated screen recording showing how you do something. It then works in the native model, covering modeling, routing, schedules, tags, dimensions, sheets and families. Pricing starts at $19/month plus usage credits ([pricing](https://archilabs.ai/pricing) , checked November 13, 2026).


### From a manufacturer PDF to a placed family


Equipment is a common example. A specification sheet arrives as a PDF, and someone has to build a family from it and place it in the project. The[equipment recording on the Desktop page](https://archilabs.ai/desktop) shows this happening: a manufacturer PDF becomes a native Revit family placed in a project. In that recording, dimensions missing from the source were approximated, and waiting time was edited out of the video.


The approximated dimensions point to the most useful habit for this kind of work. Before anything is built, ask Desktop to tell you how it reads the sheet: which model variant, which units, and how much detail you need for coordination. Spec sheets often cover several sizes in one table, and the wrong row looks perfectly reasonable once it's modeled. If a dimension isn't in the PDF, ask for it to be flagged as missing or clearly marked as approximate. A tidy-looking box that hides a guess will cause problems later.


When the family is placed, check it the way you'd check one made by a colleague. Look at it in plan and section, confirm the key dimensions against the PDF, and make sure the parameters your schedules use are filled in. Our[manufacturer-specification verification guide](https://archilabs.ai/posts/manufacturer-pdf-revit-equipment-verification) goes into this check in more detail.


### When the equipment changes


The next revision is where a family proves its worth. If the approved unit changes size, ask whether the change will edit the existing type, which affects every instance of that type in the model, or create a new type for this one unit. Either can be right, but you should decide before the change is made. Afterwards, look at the other instances that share the type and check the schedule for duplicates.


Your project can stay on Revit 2026 while you try this. Bring a real spec sheet and a copy of the model to an[ArchiLabs Desktop walkthrough](https://archilabs.ai/desktop) and see how it handles your own equipment.
